label: attack-56-demand_skeptic
system:
You are one member of a red team. You have been given ONE attack surface and you may not stray from it. You have not seen the author's reasoning and you do not want to; you see only the idea and the evidence.

Your job is to kill the idea on your surface. A weak attack wastes everyone's time. If your surface genuinely does not apply, say so with verdict "abstain" rather than inventing a weak objection; an abstention is not a survival.

Output JSON only.
user:
YOUR SURFACE — demand_skeptic:
Nobody actually wants this. The pain is stated, not felt. People say they want it and do not change behaviour. Attack the evidence itself.

IDEA
{
  "id": 56,
  "title": "Binder Scan",
  "unlock": "A vision-capable model now runs entirely on the phone at zero marginal cost, so reading a printed or handwritten recipe page, pulling out ingredients and quantities and building the week's list costs nothing per household and works with no account and no cloud bill.",
  "pain": "Households cooking from recipes found online print them into a binder and hand-write the grocery list every week because the recipes carry no structured ingredient data.",
  "audience": "Parents of school-age children who cook weeknight dinners from a printed recipe binder",
  "mechanic": "capture_and_answer",
  "wedge": "Photograph the four or five recipe pages picked for this week straight out of the binder and get back one combined shopping list with quantities added together and duplicates merged, ready before the Saturday shop.",
  "moat": "accumulated_personal_corpus",
  "model": "one_time_purchase",
  "loop": "shareable_artifact",
  "kill": [
    "Fewer than 50% of first-time users photograph a second recipe page within 7 days of the first.",
    "On-device extraction gets quantities or ingredient names wrong on more than 5% of lines across a 500-page audit of printed web recipes and handwritten cards, since a list you have to re-check by hand is the hand-written list again.",
    "Fewer than 20% of households scan 10 or more pages in the first 60 days, meaning no personal corpus forms and there is nothing to stay for.",
    "Under 3% of installs convert to the paid unlock by day 45."
  ],
  "why_not_obvious": "Not absorbable: it sits on paper the household already owns rather than on calendar, email or contacts, and the lock-in is their own digitised binder including handwritten family cards that exist nowhere else; the obvious suggestion for this audience is a recipe app with its own catalogue, which is precisely what they rejected when they printed the pages out.",
  "why_now": "End to end: the specific paid task was a meal-planning service or a household cook reading the recipes and writing the combined shopping list, and an on-device vision model [2][310] now reads the page, does the quantity arithmetic and produces the finished list with nobody in the loop - the only human act is choosing which pages to photograph."
}



Return JSON:
{
  "surface": "demand_skeptic",
  "attack": "your strongest specific argument, 2-4 sentences, concrete",
  "strongest_defence": "the best answer the author could give",
  "verdict": "fatal" | "wounded" | "survived" | "abstain",
  "verdict_reason": "one sentence"
}

Use "fatal" only when the defence cannot work at all, because a fatal verdict
kills the idea outright and no other score overrides it. Use "wounded" when the
idea survives but is materially weaker. Use "survived" when your surface is
genuinely well answered.
